dedupe_keys.name: egig european gas pipeline incident data group gas transmission pipeline incident database and reports

description: EGIG is a co-operation of nineteen major gas transmission system operators in Europe that gathers data on unintentional gas releases from their pipeline transmission systems, and owns a pipeline incident database started in 1982 with records back to 1970. The scope is onshore steel gas transmission pipelines with design pressure above 15 bar, outside the fences of installations and excluding associated equipment such as valves and compressors; only incidents with an unintentional gas release count. The members collect data on about 150 thousand km of pipelines each year, for a total exposure of 5.29 million km-years, and 1,463 incidents are recorded from 1970 to 2022, analysed by primary cause such as external interference, corrosion, ground movement and construction defects. Results are published as reports, from the 5th (1970-2001, December 2002) to the 12th (December 2024). Coverage is the member operators' networks in Europe. The reports are downloadable as PDF files at no cost, but the database itself is not published. Caveats: only aggregated statistics are public, and member operators are not identified here. Simulation uses are failure frequencies and cause shares for gas pipeline fragility and risk models, including ground movement hazards. Related records: data-canada-cer-pipeline-incident-data and data-npms-national-pipeline-mapping-system cover North American pipelines.
